'''''Helianthus'' × ''laetiflorus''''', the '''cheerful sunflower'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=Hela|taxon=Helianthus'' × ''laetiflorus|access-date=21 July 2015}}</ref> or '''perennial sunflower''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[plant]] in the family of [[Asteraceae]]. It is widespread in scattered locations across much of Canada from [[Newfoundland]] to [[British Columbia]], and the central and eastern United States as far south as [[Texas]] and [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]].<ref>{{BONAP |genus=Helianthus |species=X laetiflorus |state=1}}</ref> This species is also commonly cultivated and may escape cultivation and be found in areas outside of its core range.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Helianthus x_laetiflorus in Flora of North America @ efloras.org |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250068450 |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=www.efloras.org}}</ref>

==Description==
''Helianthus'' × ''laetiflorus'' is a [[herbaceous plant]] with alternate, simple [[leaf|leaves]], on green stems. The flowers are yellow, borne in late summer.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Scoggan |first=H. J. |date=1979 |title=Part 4, Dicotyledoneae: Loasaceae to Compositae |pages=1117–1711 |encyclopedia=Flora of Canada |publisher=National Museums of Canada |place=Ottawa}}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Gleason |first=H. A. |date=1968 |title=The Sympetalous Dicotyledoneae |volume=3 |editor-first=H. A. |editor-last=Gleason |encyclopedia=New Britton and Brown Illustrated Flora of the Northeastern United States and Adjacent Canada |publisher=New York Botanical Garden}}</ref> This species is generally considered to be of hybrid origin, with the two parental species being ''[[Jerusalem artichoke|Helianthus tuberosus]]'' and ''[[Helianthus pauciflorus]]''.<ref name=":0" />
